introduction: “Whosoever among you desireth to deliver the Cause of his Lord, it behooveth him first to deliver it unto himself.” The guide keeps returning to that order, self first and others after, and then loosens it: we develop when we give the message, we are taught while teaching, and the Master who trained his pupils sits silent to hear their songs. The principle is everyone’s. Paul asks the teacher whether he teaches himself; Jesus speaks of the beam and the mote and of those who say and do not; David asks for a clean heart before he will teach transgressors; the Dhammapada and Chaucer’s parson put practice before preaching; Portia and Ophelia know how rare that is. The difficulty is also everyone’s. If only the perfected may teach, no one will; James would have few masters; and the proverb that the waterer is watered suggests that the order “first oneself” cannot be only a sequence in time.
questions: “First he wrought, and afterward he taught”; “when we give the Message, we develop ourselves.” Do readings 1 to 4 describe one order or two? How would you reconcile them?
David prays for a clean heart and then says “then will I teach transgressors thy ways”. What is “the right state” of reading 13, and how would a teacher know it?
James warns, “be not many masters”. Reading 27 hopes all will become occupied with teaching. What does each fear?
Portia can teach twenty more easily than follow her own teaching. Why do the later readings on knowledge and study (48 to 53) come after those on conduct, and could the order be reversed?
“Now it is your turn,” says reading 33, and John has “greater works than these shall he do”. What does a teacher’s withdrawal teach?

outside.why: Whoever would deliver the Cause must “first … deliver it unto himself”. Paul’s question to the teacher of the law: thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself?
Chaucer’s poor parson is the English picture of it: first he wrought, and afterward he taught.
Test knowledge in oneself, to see whether it is practical or “merely theoretical”. Portia: I can easier teach twenty what were good to be done, than be one of the twenty to follow mine own teaching.
The proverb Jesus expects to hear from his own town says the same thing in three words: Physician, heal thyself.
First educate one’s own self, “then starts in the education of others”. The Dhammapada: let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others.
“When we give the Message, we develop ourselves.” He that watereth shall be watered also himself. If teaching is how the teacher learns, how complete must the self-teaching be before one begins?
Teach “by deeds and conduct”. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
Exalted thoughts that never reach action “remain useless”. Claudius rising from prayer: my words fly up, my thoughts remain below; words without thoughts never to heaven go.
James says of belief what the reading says of exalted thought: faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
“All the people of the world look at us to see how we act.” Ye are our epistle, known and read of all men.
Do not treat the Cause as child’s play. Of the teachers in Moses’ seat: they say, and do not.
Cling to virtue, trustworthiness and piety. Be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Associate with all; the ignorant are to be taught, the sick healed. They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
He served the disciples “in order to teach them that they must also serve”. I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
The teacher “must first find himself in the right state”. David asks for a clean heart and a right spirit, and only then says: then will I teach transgressors thy ways.
First cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.
Live among the others with humility, mostly silent. Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak.
A heart on fire will warm others. Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?
Take no breath without purpose. Paul trains himself like a runner: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.
Women must be able “by themselves and unaided” to expound every word. Philip the evangelist had four daughters which did prophesy.

The pastoral letter says: I suffer not a woman to teach, but to be in silence. The reading asks women to expound every word unaided. What has to change in a community for the second sentence to replace the first?
Be armed with proofs. Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you.
Learn the proofs from one who knows them. Apollos, eloquent and mighty in the scriptures, is taken aside by Aquila and Priscilla, who expound the way more perfectly.
Advance in English, for it will be needed. I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also.
Classes to teach the young how to teach. Commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
The education of children is among the most excellent services. Train up a child in the way he should go.

“The perfect human must engage in educating and teaching all.” James: my brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. Who is fit to teach, on his account, and who on the reading’s?
The purpose of a divine law is the education of the race, all mankind as pupils. The law was our schoolmaster.
“I am thy instructor.” Henceforth I call you not servants; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.
“You are the candle which I have lighted with my own hands.” Men do not light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick.
“I have sung my songs … Now it is your turn.” He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.
Give thanks for the one who guided you. Paul recalls the faith that dwelt first in Timothy’s grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice.
Even if the letter has no effect, continue. In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand.
A teacher must never ask for money. Freely ye have received, freely give.
And the believers provide for the traveller of their own accord. Carry neither purse, nor scrip; for the labourer is worthy of his hire.
“In movements there is life.” The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
Confer new existence upon “mouldering, dead bodies”. Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.

Those who join a campaign must first look to their own lives. Ophelia to her brother: do not, as some ungracious pastors do, show me the steep and thorny way to heaven, whiles he himself the primrose path of dalliance treads.
An adequate knowledge of the Cause is indispensable. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
To be effective, be better informed. They have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.
That the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
While teaching, the friends must themselves be taught. When for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again.

shortfall: A dozen readings are practical notes to particular people (where to stay, whom to write to, how to arrange a children’s class) or brief wishes; they were left without companions.
